name: Redensity
lead: Redensity is a name used by Teoxane for hyaluronic acid (HA) products, including RHA Redensity (a 'resilient' HA filler) and Teosyal PureSense Redensity 1 and 2.[1][2][3] They are used to soften lines around the mouth and smile, and to fill the hollow under the eye (the tear trough), so the face looks smoother and more rested without surgery.[1][3]

A randomised, evaluator-blinded multicenter study of RHA Redensity for moderate-to-severe dynamic perioral rhytides ran for 52 weeks against a no-treatment control; at week 8 the responder rate by a proprietary scale was 80.7 percent with treatment against 7.8 percent for control, and 66 percent of treated participants were still responders at week 52.[1] A prospective observational study of Redensity 2 in the periorbital region reported real-world efficacy and safety in 136 enrolled subjects, with Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale improvement above 70 percent for the tear trough and other periorbital indications.[3]

The name covers different products: RHA Redensity is the injectable for dynamic lines, Teosyal Redensity 2 is used for the tear trough, and Redensity 1 is a non-crosslinked skin-quality gel that has also been tested in the laboratory as a cell carrier in burn management.[3][4][5]

chain: HA gel is injected into the skin around the mouth or under the eye
The gel adds support and hydration
Shallower lines or a smoother tear trough, with a more rested look
angle.text: People get Redensity treatments to soften perioral lines and smile lines or to reduce under-eye hollows. The trial results describe improvement scores at weeks to a year, and clinicians can dissolve the gel with hyaluronidase if needed.

paras: RHA Redensity is described as a resilient HA filler made with a process intended to preserve HA's natural structure so the gel stretches and returns with facial movement, making it suited to dynamic areas such as the perioral region.[1][13] A 2026 paper on a newer RHA gel compares it against the existing US-approved and CE-marked RHA fillers (RHA 1 to 4 in Europe and RHA Redensity, RHA 2, RHA 3 and RHA Dynamic Volume in the US), describing a crosslinking approach that avoids high chemical modification.[13]

Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 is described as having a ten-year record for the tear trough, and Teosyal Redensity [I] is a non-stabilised HA gel combined with 14 bioactive ingredients (amino acids, antioxidants, minerals and vitamins) used for skin-quality treatment.[3][5]

Wikipedia describes HA as one of the most common filler materials because it is found naturally in vertebrates and is biodegradable; most HA fillers are crosslinked, usually with BDDE, which slows enzymatic breakdown and lengthens how long they last, and HA gives immediate volume rather than stimulating collagen.[12] In the US fillers are regulated as medical devices and must be injected by a provider, while many more are on the market in Europe where a CE mark does not require demonstration of efficacy, according to the same article.[12]

The perioral region is highly mobile, so lines around the mouth change with speech and expression. The 52-week trial (NCT03092219, n=202) used the Perioral Rhytids Severity Rating Scale and the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale rated by blinded evaluators, plus self-assessment with FACE-Q.[1][6] Most adverse events were common treatment responses after perioral injection.[1] Anaesthetic-containing versions have been tested in registered studies.[10][11]

In the periorbital observational study, 958 initial injections were given to 136 participants, of which 451 used Redensity 2: tear trough 89, palpebromalar groove 61, outer canthus 45, crow's feet 38 and brow 19.[3] A separate registered trial compared RHA Redensity Eye against no treatment for infra-orbital hollows (NCT04577898, n=248), and a micro-needle device trial tested Redensity [I] on crow's feet.[7][8]

A retrospective controlled ultrasound study of 20 women aged 30 to 42 gave a single cannula-delivered injection of Redensity [I] in the midface, comparing with seven untreated controls, and reported a significant increase in skin density on ultrasound at 3 to 4 weeks.[5] Other registered work covers radial cheek lines and neck and smile lines.[9][14] Laboratory work on non-crosslinked Redensity 1 reported support of keratinocyte and fibroblast viability and collagen deposition as a possible cell carrier for burn wounds.[4]

The 52-week randomised perioral study compared RHA Redensity with no treatment.[1] A prospective observational study assessed Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 in tear trough and other periorbital areas in routine practice.[3] A retrospective controlled ultrasound study examined cannula-assisted delivery of an HA-based hydrogel for facial skin density.[5]

Registered trials include perioral rhytids,[6] infra-orbital hollows versus no treatment,[7] crow's feet with a micro-needle device,[8] radial cheek lines,[9] neck lines, perioral lines and smiling lines,[14] and anaesthetic-containing versions.[10][11]

Wikipedia lists common effects of HA fillers as bruising, redness, pain and itching, with infection, allergic reactions and lumps less common, and vascular embolization causing blindness or skin necrosis as rare but serious events.[12] In a 2023 in-vitro study, 21 HA fillers were exposed to recombinant human hyaluronidase; RHA 1/Redensity was among the least resistant to dissolving, while RHA 4 was among the most resistant.[2] Clinical safety in the Redensity trials is reported as common treatment responses and adverse events.[1][3]

timeline.event: Registered trial of Redensity [I] with a micro-needle device for crow's feet begins.[8]
RHA Redensity perioral rhytids trial begins (NCT03092219).[6]
Trial of RHA Redensity Eye for infra-orbital hollows begins.[7]
Periorbital real-world and cannula skin-density studies published.[3][5]

card.summary: Teoxane's 'Redensity' hyaluronic acid products (RHA Redensity and Teosyal Redensity) for lines and under-eye hollows; includes a randomised 52-week perioral trial.
card.aka: RHA Redensity, Teosyal PureSense Redensity, Redensity 1, Redensity 2
card.note: Name covers several different products (a filler for dynamic lines and a under-eye gel); evidence differs by product.

quick.overview:
Redensity is a name used by Teoxane for hyaluronic acid products. RHA Redensity is a 'resilient' HA filler designed for dynamic areas of the face, studied for perioral lines and infra-orbital hollows; Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 is used for the tear trough under the eyes.

In aesthetic discussion it appears mostly in connection with under-eye and lip-line treatment.
quick.mechanism: The gels are injected under or into the skin where hyaluronic acid adds support and hydration. The RHA range is described as made with a process meant to preserve HA structure so the gel stretches and returns with facial movement.
quick.risks: Typical reported effects of HA fillers include swelling, bruising and lumps; vascular and delayed inflammatory reactions are rarer. HA fillers can be dissolved with hyaluronidase, and a 2023 study tested response of 21 fillers.
